purpose: Training-seed robustness of the alarm-matched development comparison, not a revision of the failed original continuation gate
changes: Only initialization and sampling seed change. Keep the existing 500000 fit rows, fit-only scaler, fixed loss denominator, client ownership, architecture, updater settings and grouped calibration/audit split. Within each seed use the same initialization across all arms and identical client sample multisets across federated arms.
evaluation: Final endpoints only. Calibrate each model on the same calibration benign rows using the existing strict-margin order statistic. No audit retuning, checkpoint selection, learning-rate search or early stopping.
reporting: Report both new seeds separately, paired differences and all-class recall at every target. Also describe seeds 7,17,27 with arithmetic mean, sample standard deviation and range. Seed 7 remains discovery evidence, not a third new replication. No significance or equivalence claim from three seeds.
interpretation: A consistent positive shared-versus-FedAvg macro-F1 difference in both new seeds at the primary target, with realized FAR differences within the fixed tolerance, supports studying communication reduction. Report central gaps without rounding a failed two-point gap into a pass. This is not a new final-success gate and does not override the previous screen.
limits: Previously examined training-derived development data and one fixed historical non-IID partition. This tests training-seed sensitivity, not partition sensitivity, independent capture generalization or privacy. Shared Adam communicates 20 times as often as this FedAvg convention. Payload estimates exclude transport and security overhead.
